name: Moderate diet (mitāhāra)
method_summary: Eating smooth, sweet, wholesome food, offered to Śiva, leaving a quarter (GS: half food, a quarter water, a quarter air) of the stomach empty; avoiding pungent, sour, salty, heating and stale foods, alcohol, meat and fish; milk and ghee at the start of practice (HYP 1.58–63, 2.14; GS 5.16–25; DYŚ 64–66).

warnings.text: Whoever begins yoga without moderate diet gets various diseases and his yoga does not succeed.
Overeating is the first of the six things that destroy yoga.

name: The sevenfold yoga of the pot (ghaṭastha-yoga)
method_summary: The Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā's whole course: cleansing acts, postures, mudrās, withdrawal, breath-control, meditation and samādhi, each producing one quality of the 'pot' (purity, firmness, steadiness, calm, lightness, perception of the self, non-attachment).

name: Gross, luminous and subtle meditation (Gheraṇḍa)
method_summary: Gross: visualize a jewel island in an ocean of nectar in the heart with the chosen deity (or the guru in the lotus of the crown); luminous: meditate on kuṇḍalinī as a flame at the root, the navel sun, or the praṇava-light between the brows; subtle: by śāmbhavī, on awakened kuṇḍalinī (GS 6.1–22).

warnings.text: Subtle meditation is secret, hard even for the gods to obtain (a warning of secrecy).

name: The indications of layayoga (saṅketa)
method_summary: Dissolving the mind by fixing attention on an 'indication': meditating on the void at all times, gazing at the nose-tip or between the brows, meditating on the back of the head or on the big toes, lying relaxed like a corpse in solitude — Ādinātha taught eight crore such (DYŚ 14–24).

name: Mantrayoga of the haṭha texts
method_summary: Placing the mātṛkā letters on the limbs and repeating a mantra (DYŚ 11); the Śiva Saṃhitā adds a mantra practice with seed-syllables meditated in the centres (5.188ff). Counts of repetition are not recorded here.

warnings.text: Mantrayoga is the lowest yoga, for the dull; mantra-sādhana is listed among the obstacles at the start of practice.

name: The mindless yoga (amanaska / rājayoga of the Amanaska)
method_summary: Letting the mind rest without object, with a steady gaze that fixes on nothing, by the guru's grace, until the mind dissolves and the breath stops of itself (Amanaska 2); without the laborious methods of haṭha.
signs_of_progress: stillness of body like a log; breath ceasing; neither sleep nor waking (Amanaska 2)

name: Piercing the six centres (ṣaṭcakra-bheda) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. The Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa describes rousing kuṇḍalinī by a method learned from the guru and leading her up through the six centres, dissolving each element into the next, to union with Paramaśiva in the thousand-petalled lotus, and back. No steps are recorded.
prerequisites: initiation and instruction by a guru (ṢCN 50, 55)

warnings.text: Only by the method learned from the guru (the text's condition).

name: Cheating death (kālavañcana)
method_summary: The texts' means of postponing or conquering death: breath held in the body (HYP 2.39–40), preserving bindu and nectar, the element-concentrations that remove fear of each element (DYŚ 100–110), and (HTK) knowledge of the signs of approaching death to anticipate it.

name: Yogic departure from the body (utkrānti) — summary only
method_summary: RESTRICTED. The perfected yogin is said to be able to leave the body at will and merge in Brahman (DYŚ 115); the Haṭhatattvakaumudī has a chapter on a breath practice for it. No method is recorded.

name: Worship of one's reflection (pratīkopāsana, shadow-gazing)
method_summary: In bright sun, gazing steadily at one's own shadow and then at the sky, where one's image appears; its wholeness is read as a sign of long life and victory (SS 5.15–20).

name: Meditation with and without qualities
method_summary: Holding the breath, meditating on the chosen deity (with qualities: gives the powers) and then on the qualityless like space (gives liberation), leading to samādhi (DYŚ 111–114; GŚ 76–85).

name: The restraints and observances of the haṭha texts
method_summary: The ten yamas (non-harming, truth, non-stealing, continence, forbearance, fortitude, compassion, straightforwardness, moderate diet, purity) and ten niyamas of the interpolated HYP verses and the Yoga Yājñavalkya; the SS's list of things to avoid (3.33) and to follow (3.35); in the HYP the ethical frame is chiefly celibacy, moderate diet and renunciation (1.57).
